P1: Renamed 2026-01-14 (same arguments): Player:LoadCharacter -> LoadCharacterAsync; BadgeService:AwardBadge -> AwardBadgeAsync; MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo -> GetProductInfoAsync. The old names are deprecated but still work. Not renamed: Instance:WaitForChild and RemoteFunction:InvokeServer keep their names. The Async versions are network calls, so wrap them in pcall.
P2: Set Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server (Workspace > Server Authority; full release 2026-07-09). It forces these on: NextGenerationReplication, PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem, SignalBehavior = Deferred, StreamingEnabled and UseFixedSimulation. Client-predicted gameplay logic goes in a function registered with RunService:BindToSimulation(fn), which runs on both client and server and can be rolled back and resimulated. Read input from InputAction, not UserInputService events. Sync state through attributes. Use time() as the clock: tick(), os.time() and os.clock() do not roll back. Destroying or reparenting instances inside bound functions errors.
P3: The property is Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem. Timeline: Phase 1 (June 2026) defaults to Disabled, and you can opt in. Phase 2 (early 2027, planned) defaults to Enabled. Phase 3 (mid 2027, planned) removes the property, so IAS-based player scripts become the only option. Code at risk: anything that uses PlayerModule internals such as require(PlayerModule):GetControls(), code that relies on the old ContextActionService/UserInputService input sinking or priorities, and forked or custom PlayerScripts. Keep forks with StarterPlayer.CreateDefaultPlayerModule = Disabled. Also, binding the same key in both systems double-fires.
P4: Platform-integrated chat (Oct 2026): Roblox renders chat itself (TextChannelWindow), so a custom chat UI can no longer draw message text. TextChatMessage.Text and .Translation return "" with a warning, OnIncomingMessage and Player.Chatted get no text, and preset SendAsync messages are replaced by Quick Words. Build admin commands with TextChatCommand and keep chat tags in attributes; native prefixes and role badges are planned for Feb 2027. Timeline: opt-in testing via TextChatService.PlatformIntegratedChat (Studio) until Feb 2027. From Feb 2027 it is on by default with an opt-out, and it becomes required around May 2027 (the announcement also mentions an opt-out before March 2027). Stop building features that read message text, such as keyword triggers or chat minigames.
P5: Limits are per experience, per minute, scale with concurrent users (CCU), and are shared by every server and by Open Cloud. Write budget = 300 + 20 x CCU per minute (the base was 250 before 2026-07-29). Read = 300 + 40 x CCU, List = 300 + 2 x CCU, Remove = 300 + 40 x CCU. Per key: 4 MB/min write and 25 MB/min read throughput, with each request rounded up to the next KB. Per-server request queues hold 30 requests. Storage = 500 MB + 1 MB x lifetime users (compressed, latest versions only). UpdateAsync counts as one read plus one write. Use GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before bulk work.
P6: The crates are paid random items. Gems are bought with Robux, so crates bought with Gems are covered even for players who earned their Gems by playing. Before purchase, show every possible outcome with numeric odds that add up to 100% (rounding is OK with a disclaimer; long lists can go behind a labelled 'Info/Details' button). The Luck Potion is an odds modifier: state its exact numeric effect before purchase, and while it is active show the player's real, boosted odds. Per player, on the server: call PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync in pcall. If ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted is true, block buying crates with Robux-bought currency (offer a free or direct-sale path, or hide them). If IsPaidItemTradingAllowed is false, block trading. Fail closed on errors and never gate only on the client.

To reach Kids/Select users, the creator must be age-checked (facial estimation, or ID if 18+) and have 2-Step Verification on. They also need either two consecutive months of Roblox Plus/Premium or a refundable 1,000 Robux per-game fee. The game needs a full content-maturity questionnaire, with a Minimal or Mild rating for Kids and up to Moderate for Select. It must also pass Roblox's Kids/Select evaluation; during the trial it is 16+ only until enough engaged, age-checked players have played it (see the Audience Reach dashboard).

Daily Engagement pays 5 Robux per qualifying Active Spender per day, when they play 10+ minutes and the game is one of the first three they launch that day. Audience Expansion pays 35% of a new or returning user's first $100 of spend within their first 60 days. Payouts are Earned Robux with a hold. DevEx: the standard rate is $0.0038 per Earned Robux. The US 18+ rate, from June 8, 2026, is $0.0054 for qualifying Robux only: the buyer is a verified US adult, the purchase is a dev product, pass, subscription or private server, and the game meets the avatar rules. G1: Rules: (1) Assign ProcessReceipt once, on the server. (2) Make it idempotent per PurchaseId: record granted PurchaseIds in a DataStore (or the player's session-locked profile, saved with UpdateAsync) and skip any you have already granted. (3) Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant has been durably saved. If the player is offline, the save fails, or the data is not loaded yet, return NotProcessedYet so Roblox retries later (on rejoin). (4) Never yield forever, and wrap DataStore calls in pcall. (5) Grant only the product that matches ProductId. Charged with nothing: returning Granted even when the save errored or the player had left, or erroring in the callback. Granted twice: Roblox retries a receipt until it is acknowledged (callback timed out, the server shut down, Granted not returned after the grant), and without a PurchaseId check each retry grants again.
G2: Use UpdateAsync for any read-modify-write: incrementing, merging, session locks, and data other servers might touch. It is atomic, retries on conflict and sees the current value. SetAsync after GetAsync can overwrite newer data, which causes rollbacks and duplicated items. Use SetAsync only for blind overwrites (for example an admin restore while the player is offline). Transform rules: it gets (oldValue, keyInfo), and keyInfo is nil for a new key. Return the new value, or nil to cancel the write. It must not yield (no task.wait, other Async calls or remote invokes). It can run several times, so keep it pure and don't mutate captured live tables. Return userIds and metadata (keyInfo:GetUserIds()/GetMetadata()) or they get cleared. Check session-lock ownership inside it, and wrap the call in pcall.
G3:
Not safe. A NaN passes both comparisons (NaN < 0 and NaN > Gold are both false). inf is caught, but fractional values (0.5) and 0 are accepted. It only checks the balance, without reserving it, so the player can send many offers or spend the gold elsewhere while offers are open (duplication/race). There is also no rate limit. Fix:
```lua
local last = {}
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
  if typeof(gold) ~= "number" or gold ~= gold then return end
  if gold ~= math.floor(gold) or gold <= 0 or gold > 1e9 then return end
  local now = os.clock(); if last[player] and now - last[player] < 0.5 then return end; last[player] = now
  if gold > player.Gold.Value or hasOpenOffer(player) then return end
  player.Gold.Value -= gold -- escrow; refund on cancel
  createOffer(player, gold)
end)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)
```
Re-validate when the trade completes.
G4: The Animator overwrites Motor6D.Transform every frame on every joint that a playing track keys. Animation is applied after Heartbeat's timing slot, so a Heartbeat write is replaced by the idle pose before rendering. Write procedural offsets in RunService.PreSimulation (formerly Stepped), which runs after the animation step and before physics/render. Compose with the animated value instead of replacing it: motor.Transform = aimRotation * motor.Transform (rotation applied on top of the animation), so the idle still plays. Don't multiply cumulatively on joints the animation doesn't key, or it compounds. Edit C0/C1 instead for persistent rest-pose offsets (mount position, grip offset, a static re-aim); those aren't overwritten by animation. Don't use C0 for per-frame aim.
G5: Blending is per joint, and only tracks that key that joint compete. AnimationPriority decides it: Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2 < Action3 < Action4. Higher-priority tracks take weight first, and lower ones only get the leftover. If the swing is at Core or Movement (the default for many uploaded animations), it blends 50/50 with walk or loses. Set swingTrack.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action (before Play) or set it in the Animation Editor. Weights: within the same priority, tracks blend in proportion to weight (two at 1 = 50/50). A higher-priority track at weight 1 fully overrides lower ones on the joints it keys, and at 0.6 it leaves 40% to the lower ones. Use AdjustWeight and fade times. Also check the tool hold pose (toolnone), which keys the right arm.
G6: It's a unit-scale mismatch. FBX is centimetre-based and Blender works in metres, so with unit scale 1 a 1 m object gets written as 100 FBX units (cm). Studio reads these as studs or rescales them, giving a 100x size. Recommended FBX export: Apply Scalings = 'FBX Unit Scale' (or FBX All), Scale 1.0, Forward -Z/Up Y (Forward Z, Up Y), Apply Unit on, Apply Transform/applied transforms (Ctrl+A in Blender), Add Leaf Bones off, Path Mode Copy + Embed Textures, Bake Animation off unless exporting clips. In the Studio importer, set the matching Scale Unit (Stud/Meter) and check the size. Use a single scaling method rather than scaling twice, and don't fix it by scaling in Studio for rigs, because animation translations stay in the old units.
G7: glTF only stores mesh data. Live (unapplied) modifiers aren't in the file unless the exporter evaluates them, so you get the base mesh: half the model (no Mirror) and sharp edges (no Bevel). Fix: tick Apply Modifiers in the glTF exporter (Data > Mesh) or apply them manually. Catch: export-time Apply Modifiers bakes the whole stack, including ones you wanted live (e.g. the Armature modifier on rigs), and Blender's exporter can't apply modifiers on meshes with shape keys, which get dropped or block it. Custom normals may also change. For rigged meshes, apply Mirror and Bevel by hand on a copy and leave the exporter option off. Enable Clipping on Mirror so the seam doesn't split.
G8: Stretching: Scale on both axes follows the screen's aspect ratio, so 0.3x0.3 of a 16:9 monitor isn't the same shape on a 19.5:9 phone or a 4:3 tablet. Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (e.g. AspectRatio 1) or use SizeConstraint = RelativeYY, or use Offset sizes plus one UIScale computed from the viewport, with min/max via UISizeConstraint. Notch/top bar: the gui is drawn into the unsafe area or the top-bar inset. Fix: on the ScreenGui set ScreenInsets = CoreUISafeInsets (clears the notch and Roblox top bar), keep IgnoreGuiInset = false, use SafeAreaCompatibility = None for new guis, and offset by GuiService.TopbarInset if needed. Put full-bleed decorative art in a separate ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = None.

```lua
BuyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
  if typeof(itemId) ~= "string" or typeof(quantity) ~= "number" then return end
  if quantity ~= quantity or quantity % 1 ~= 0 or quantity < 1 or quantity > 99 then return end
  local item = ITEMS[itemId]; if not item then return end
  local now = os.clock()

  last[player] = now
  local data = getData(player); if not data then return end -- server-held profile

  data.Coins -= cost
  data.Items[itemId] = (data.Items[itemId] or 0) + quantity

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)
```
The price and balance come from the server, never the client; types, NaN, integer and bounds are checked; and calls are rate-limited.

T4: On the client, FireServer automatically sends the firing player as the first parameter on the server. Passing LocalPlayer yourself shifts the arguments: the server gets (player, LocalPlayer, 50), so `amount` is the Player instance, and Instance + 1 errors. Fix the client to `remote:FireServer(50)`. Keep the server as `function(player, amount)`, but validate it: `if typeof(amount) ~= "number" or amount ~= amount then return end`. Never trust a client-sent player argument; use the automatic one.
T5:
In Studio solo, the local player can join before the server Script has connected PlayerAdded (for example after a slow require or a WaitForChild that yields first), so the event already fired for that player and is missed. Live servers start before anyone joins, which hides the bug. Standard fix: connect first, then loop over players already in the game:
```lua
local function onPlayerAdded(player) --[[ create leaderstats ]] end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p) end
```
Also don't yield before connecting.

T8: Your game has mesh streaming / improved LoDs on (Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs = Enabled, and Default becomes Enabled as the rollout progresses). In that mode the engine generates cloud LoDs and streams meshes automatically, and MeshPart.RenderFidelity is ignored entirely. So Precise does nothing, and distant meshes still swap to lower LoDs. Studio can look different from live because of the setting or the rollout state. Check the effective value of the Workspace property. Fixes: set the property to Disabled if you really need fixed fidelity (temporary, as it is being phased in); otherwise budget triangles at the source and design for LoD (Model.LevelOfDetail, sensible poly counts). Leave RenderFidelity on Automatic; Precise is an anti-pattern anyway.
